recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Foot in Both Worlds", "body": "Michael Wann opens by explaining why he is still online after vowing to walk away from the technosphere, a system he says was designed to be fun and addictive. He has stopped one-on-one video calls and moved much of his sharing to an audio-only show with Mark, while preparing for his first big in-person event in years. Chance answers that he needs a foot in both worlds for now, and that the real question is which foot carries the weight. He describes his remote tuning fork and divination sessions as proof, in his view, that life force energy connects people even through artificial channels."}, {"title": "The Internet and the Rewilding Response", "body": "Mike points out that the internet grew out of the Department of Defense, and argues that the people who sold the idea brought expertise in behavioral control, which he says is the very definition of cybernetics. He says he was raised inside that world through his schooling, jobs and family, which gives him an intimate view of what he now wants to step away from. Rewilding consciousness, as he describes it, is not moving to the wilderness but purposefully questioning inherited frames such as months, base ten numbers, the tropical zodiac and chakras, without throwing the baby out with the bath water."}, {"title": "From Feedback Loops to Feedback Webs", "body": "Chance shares a friend's account of orgone earth pipes planted near 5G towers across Arizona, which he links to an unusually rainy monsoon season and to Triops reappearing in the desert. He wonders whether life is a frequency, with fear narrowing the bandwidth of what people can perceive and love widening it again. He proposes feedback webs in place of cybernetic feedback loops, pointing to the body, where every organ talks to every other, and to Qigong, where imagining the energy during each movement slowly becomes a felt inner language all our own."}, {"title": "False Realities Must Be Fed", "body": "Mike defines a false reality as any reality that has to be fed to exist, and says the cultural one sustains itself as a closed cybernetic loop, so that everything around a person repeats the same story. Rewilding, in his telling, means stepping outside it while admitting a blind spot, and he argues that when enough people believe and act on an idea, the world really does change. Chance adds his own reading of the word cyber as a segmented psyche, contrasts I Ching hexagrams 11 and 12, peace and standstill, and argues that the Gregorian calendar chops a lunar cycle into artificial segments."}, {"title": "Seeing the Cave as It Collapses", "body": "Mike argues that this moment, with long-held societal promises falling away, gives everyone alive an unusual chance to see the edges of the false reality they were born into, and he compares that seeing to Plato's cave and to the finger that points at the moon. Chance describes using L rods to dowse the size of each chakra's field before his tuning fork work, which he says speeds up his sessions. Mike says that practice shows how people have been sold the idea they must go outside themselves for knowledge, when the body and its higher senses are enough."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Build-Your-Own Time Keeping Solutions for Exiting Simulations...
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Michael Wann, the Susquehanna Sage himself, triumphantly returns to InnerVerse for a third fantastic flow state. This time around we discuss the nature of artificial reality, how it works, and how to reconnect to the larger, truer reality of nature. Full of surprises, this conversation shows how fun it can be to break out of the molds that the parasite masters have provided for us, and find the rhythm and feeling of real life once again.
